newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Mark Bradtke has returned to Australia after a season in the USA National Basketball League with the Philadelphia 76ers. He is undecided about returning to the USA professional circuit and is considering re-joining the Melbourne Tigers in the Australian competition. Page 18.

Tom Raudonikis is today expected to be confirmed as coach of the New South Wales team in this season's State of Origin series, the premier competition event for the Australian Rugby League. Raudonikis will take over the position from vacating coach Phil Gould. Page 20.

Australian swimmer Susan O'Neill, Olympic champion in the women's 200m butterfly at the Atlanta Games, has announced she will defend her title at the Sydney 2000 Olympics. O'Neill is No.3 on the world all-time list for 200m butterfly. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian basketball is experiencing a turbulent season with former champions, the Sydney Kings, having a disastrous season so far. Sydney Kings' coach Alan Black is hoping to reverse the team's 0-2 win-loss record at Friday's match against the Perth Widcats despite being hampered by a major injury toll among players. Page 51.

The Australian racing industry is adjusting to the move to privatise the New South Wales TAB. The state's racing industry has expressed concern over the pace of the reforms. Furthermore the industry is worried over moves by the Australian Jockey Club to increase rents for Randwick stables, a major forum for Australian racing. Page 51.

Australian swimming is set for a major overhaul. Long established stars like Kieren Perkins, Scott Miller and Sam Riley will face fierce competition in the run up to the Sydney 2000 Olympics from the rising generation of swimmers which performed spectacularly at the recent world short-course championships. Page 51.
THE AGE

A large field of international drivers including German world cup touring car winner Frank Biela, are expected to compete in Australia's premier motor racing event, the 35th Bathurst 1000 on October 5. Page B6.

Captain of the Australian Davis Cup tennis team, John Newcombe, has predicted that world No.1 player Peter Sampras will join the American team playing against Australia in the title's semi-final to be held in September. Page B6.

Australian Football League (AFL) superstar Gary Ablett is expected to re-join his old team Geelong very soon. Ablett has been sidelined since a knee injury in round one of this season, but is now confident he can resume playing without risking permanent amage. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian teenager 17-year-old Todd Kelly will attempt his second consecutive victory in the Australian Formula Ford Championship this weekend. Kelly is part of the Holden "Young Lions" V8 Supercar squad and is confident of his chances of victory with his new car. Page 81.

The Australian Football League (AFL) will today hear a historic first hearing of a racial abuse charge. Reserve player for the Western bulldogs Todd Curley will face the AFL Tribunal to answer charges that he racially abused Melbourne Aboriginal player David Cockatoo-Collins. Page 84.

Australian Football League (AFL) commentators are becoming increasingly concerned about the high injury rate in the sport. Currently one in every five of the AFL's 672 listed players are either injured, ill or recovering. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australia's premier lawn bowler Kevin Kerrow recorded a triumphant win against world champion Tony Allcock in the opening match of the Jack High tournament yesterday. Kerrow defeated Allcock 4-9 9-6 9-4 and is now favourite to take out the championshp. Page 86.

Australian Super League Captain Laurie Daley has announced he will donate his A$5,000 playing fee for the Anzac Day (25 April) Test to the Kokoda Track Memorial Walk. The latter commemorates the service of Australian serviceman in Papua New Guinea in World War Two. Page 90.

An Australian judge has criticised the level of violence among the Australian Rugby League codes. Justice Bill Lee warned yesterday that players could expect to face criminal charges if they injured each other during matches. Page 96.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
